listings.summary: Explore Advance Wars Recompiled and follow the upstream project for requirements, downloads and setup.

steps.title: Prepare upstream or keep an existing game build
steps.instruction: Use your own Advance Wars USA Rev 1 original with the upstream Windows alpha guide. Run Setup.cmd deliberately; it records setup.log, skips completed work and can be resumed. The generated Advance Wars (recomp).cmd launches the prepared game. For native registration, choose build/Release/AWRE.exe, use the prepared project root as working directory and game/aw.gba as the argument in Change launch details. Compiler tools are not the game; the reviewed alpha has no audio.

steps.title: Keep your files and update through upstream
steps.instruction: Use a separate folder you control and retain your working copy. An existing native player can use Portcove’s non-owning registration after the read-only executable review; choose Play separately. You or upstream keep runtime updates, original files, generated data, saves and settings. Portcove does not replace, back up or roll back this external runtime. Follow the selected upstream version’s instructions when changing it.

listings.name: Shadow of the Colossus — 2018 PS4 remake (ShadowOfTheColossus-PC)
listings.summary: Upstream route: Upstream runtime package for ShadowOfTheColossus-PC; use own game files per documented setup, with upstream/player owning installation and runtime replacement. Observed release artifacts are evidence, not operational package selection or Portcove support. Limits: Upstream only: Upstream claims ending/credits. AMD fix not confirmed on physical hardware; no Portcove playthrough or inherited fork qualification. Primary parent for row37 optimized fork. Upstream start-to-end claim; AMD fixes not physically tested. Compare existing PS4 runtime ownership, not PS2/PS3 editions. Upstream platforms: Windows10/11 PS4 layer, EU CUSA08809v1.01. US support belongs to Oussama fork; own console audio modules required. Original data: Own PS4 ShadowOfColossus Bluepoint2018 EU CUSA08809v1.01 game dump with eboot.bin,sce_module,sce_sys. Sound requires owner-dumped decrypted libSceNgs2.sprx and libSceUlt.sprx; silent without them. Modules are Sony firmware, excluded from package. US support belongs to Oussama fork extension, not established for parent. Portcove setup/gameplay not verified.

listings.name: MechCommander 2 / mc2 (alariq)
listings.summary: Explore MechCommander 2 / mc2 (alariq) and follow the upstream project for requirements, downloads and setup.

steps.title: Use the complete Windows player
steps.instruction: The official Windows x64 ZIP includes mc2.exe, its libraries and game data. Keep the complete package together. For an existing copy, select mc2.exe in the extracted mc2-win64 folder and use that folder as the working directory. Save launch details, then choose Play separately. The selected release has no Linux player archive; upstream provides separate Linux source/data build instructions. Follow all included notices: project code and components have their own licenses, and Microsoft’s Art Assets grant limits their use and distribution to noncommercial purposes.

steps.title: Back up the external saves
steps.instruction: Normal saves use .mechcommander2/savegame under your Windows user-profile folder. Linux uses that path under XDG_CONFIG_HOME when set, otherwise HOME. Close the game and back up that external user-data folder separately. Keep options.cfg, options.cfg.old, orgprefs.cfg, data/multiplayer and any custom data locations with the copy you use. External profiles and custom paths are outside Portcove backups.

steps.title: Keep an existing copy recoverable
steps.instruction: For a copy you registered yourself, you or upstream provide updates. Extract a new official player separately and keep the working copy. Follow upstream guidance for settings and custom content; copying old generated texture or geometry caches over a new package can replace its new files. Registration leaves every external file untouched.

listings.name: Alone in the Dark: The New Nightmare / Alexbeav PSXRecomp
listings.summary: Upstream PlayStation setup package using your own matching disc and any required BIOS. Finish generation with upstream; that external copy keeps its own runtime updates and player data.

steps.title: Download the upstream setup package
steps.instruction: Extract the complete official setup ZIP for your system into a separate writable folder you control. This is a setup package: its launcher prepares the game from your own matching disc through upstream generation/build. On Linux, follow the selected version’s prerequisites, including CMake, Ninja, Python 3 and a C/C++ compiler where required; bundled Windows tools do not supply Linux tools. Downloading and extracting do not run a launcher, compiler or game. Native setup and gameplay remain unqualified by this handoff.

steps.title: Supply the matching original files
steps.instruction: Follow the upstream guide for the version you downloaded. Use your own original in its supported image representation, keeping a CUE and every referenced track together when required, and supply your own BIOS whenever that guide requires it. Use both supported European discs and your own supported Europe SCPH BIOS. The included OpenBIOS supports setup only. Upstream documents independent disc startup; natural gameplay disc switching is not established by this handoff.

steps.title: Finish upstream setup, then add the player
steps.instruction: Deliberately open the supported upstream launcher when you are ready to generate/build from your own files. Follow that version’s completed-player instructions and keep its runtime/compiler companions together. In Portcove choose the resulting native game executable or supported upstream launcher with its supplied working folder. If setup created it elsewhere, select that location. Saving launch details and Play are separate Portcove actions. You or upstream manage runtime updates, original files, saves and settings; these external files are outside Portcove-managed backups. Keep a working copy and its data before changing versions.

Portcove setup/gameplay not verified.

steps.title: Finish setup in the upstream Android app
steps.instruction: This fork’s published APK is for Android, specifically the AYN Thor dual-screen UZDoom route. Install this fork’s APK on the Android device, open its launcher deliberately, and select your own compatible Doom-family IWAD/content through the UZDoom setup. Other engines named in the inherited parent README have been excluded from this fork; do not prepare Doom RPG, Wolfenstein RPG or another parent engine for this APK.

steps.title: Keep your data when changing versions
steps.instruction: Keep your selected IWADs, mods and actual Android app data backed up before changing versions. This fork’s reviewed guide does not establish an exact save/export location. Updates and device setup belong to the upstream Android app, outside Portcove runtime backup and rollback.

listings.summary: Build Burnout 2 from your own US Xbox disc through upstream setup, keeping its saves and imported music.

steps.title: Prepare a player with upstream setup
steps.instruction: The official Installation.zip is a source and setup kit, not a ready-made player. On Windows, install the upstream LLVM 22.1-or-newer, Visual Studio 2026 C++/Windows SDK, CMake 4.2-or-newer, Git and Ninja prerequisites, extract the kit into a separate retained source folder, then deliberately run Build.cmd and select your own US Xbox XISO (.iso or .xiso). A full-disc dump needs upstream conversion first. The builder acquires dependencies and builds the player. Portcove does not run it during discovery.

steps.title: Register the completed player
steps.instruction: When the upstream build succeeds, use Open game folder and choose b2.exe with that folder as its working directory in Portcove. Save the launch details, then choose Play separately. For Linux use upstream Install.desktop; macOS uses Install.command and its Xcode/macOS prerequisites. These experimental native platforms have separate dependency/build instructions; Windows package inspection does not qualify them. Keep source, build and data folders together, and rerun upstream setup after moving them.

steps.title: Back up and rebuild when updating
steps.instruction: You or upstream own the runtime, generated game files and updates. Before updating, close the game and builder and back up data/user, data/local/settings.cfg and any data/local/custom-music beside the player. Extract updated source over the retained source folder while keeping build and data, then deliberately rerun the platform setup with your own XISO. Keep the old working copy and originals recoverable. Portcove external registration leaves files untouched and supplies no managed Update, Backup or Rollback.

listings.name: Cave Story / doukutsu-rs (doukutsu-rs)
listings.summary: Prepare a separate Cave Story player with your own supported data and preserve the chosen edition’s saves.

steps.title: Prepare a separate Cave Story folder
steps.instruction: Keep your current game and store installation. For the original freeware edition, put the downloaded doukutsu-rs Windows executable beside a copy of your Doukutsu.exe and data folder; first launch extracts the additional original resources. For supported Cave Story+ editions, use your own data folder as described by upstream. The 2026 Steam remaster is not established by this guide, and remastered saves are incompatible with original-version saves. If an Epic copy contains the stray opengl32.dll described upstream, apply its fix only to your separate prepared copy.

steps.title: Add the prepared player
steps.instruction: On Windows, select the downloaded x86_64 doukutsu-rs executable and its containing game folder as the working directory. Save launch details, then choose Play separately. Keep its matching data folder in place. Linux publishes a standalone x86_64 ELF, and the Mac downloads contain separate Intel or Apple Silicon app bundles; follow the linked platform instructions for those instead of treating the Windows download as an installer.

steps.title: Keep the chosen edition and user data
steps.instruction: You own updates to this external copy. Prepare another version separately and keep your current player, original data and saves until it works. The engine normally uses the operating system’s doukutsu-rs user-data folder, or a sibling user folder in portable mode. Its Advanced menu can open the user-data folder; keep a separate backup of it, including settings.json and saves, before changing versions or editions. Portcove does not back up, roll back or delete this external game/data tree.

steps.title: Import your own game on first Play
steps.instruction: The official Windows x64 ZIP is portable and has no installer. Choose InfiniteUndiscoveryRecomp.exe and keep its DLLs and notices together. steps.title: Keep each content profile together
steps.instruction: The complete portable folder holds setup.json and separate USA, USA-UNDUB, EUROPE, JAPAN and ASIA profiles. Close the game before updates or copying data. Keep interrupted import/staging folders recoverable and consult upstream; do not merge different editions. Backups can include large original-game files and DLC, so keep them private. The separate IU Save Bridge companion is optional and is not run by Portcove.

steps.title: Update an existing copy safely
steps.instruction: For a copy you register yourself, you or upstream provide updates. Extract a new official player into a separate folder, keep the working copy, and follow the selected release’s instructions for carrying its complete compatible content profiles and setup.json. Do not copy old runtime DLLs or shader caches over the replacement. Runtime rollback does not rewind saves or guarantee that older software can read them. The selected release-tag documentation had not tested the Disc 1 to Disc 2 transition. Later upstream documentation at 614a0a0ebd72103fce8aaa52c715d847b703a53e reports repeated successful transitions, while complete Disc 2 progression and a full playthrough remain unverified and a Vesplume Tower / Orb of Patience softlock remains under investigation. steps.title: Back up your actual save folder
steps.instruction: Normal cartridge saves (.sav) and optional state slots (.stateN) follow your selected original game file, usually outside the installation. steps.title: Keep your choices and mod versions when updating
steps.instruction: If Library identifies this copy as Portcove-managed, use its compatible stable update. Complete mods/packages/<id>/<version> packages coexist with new upstream defaults; your mod state is retained without choosing a new default for you. A changed package using the same ID/version requires reviewing the reported copies separately before retrying. Mods remain player/upstream-owned code: preservation does not authenticate them or establish compatibility. Generated executable caches and diagnostics stay with each runtime and are regenerated. steps.title: Prepare your own disc before Play
steps.instruction: Before Play, prepare game-data beside the new player from your own Ratchet & Clank (2002) NTSC-U SCUS-97199 version 1.00 disc. Use a 2048-byte-sector .iso; BIN, CHD and another region are not accepted by this extractor. Open the installed runtime folder and deliberately run its bundled rerac-extract.exe on Windows, or ./rerac-extract on Linux/macOS: identify --iso "<your ISO>", then extract --iso "<your ISO>" --out game-data, then verify --out game-data. Wait for successful completion and verification; allow about 4.5 GB for extracted disc data plus prepared caches. Keep the complete runtime folder and its assets/shaders together. After successful extraction and verification, return to Portcove to continue. A separately registered copy keeps its explicit Play action. Portcove never runs this extractor during discovery. The upstream runtime refuses missing, incomplete or incompatible extraction; wait for successful extraction and verification before Play.

steps.title: Use the guided launcher when you prefer
steps.instruction: For guided ISO selection, progress, verification, re-extraction and version management, use the official ReRAC Launcher linked by Open setup guide. Its published Windows MSI, Linux AppImage and macOS disk images are separate from these game ZIPs. Follow its Version Management and Install via ISO flow, then register your prepared player with its real data directory, or register the launcher deliberately if you want its own interface. That copy’s runtime updates belong to the launcher. The project’s older README statement that nothing has been released does not describe the currently published launcher packages. Mod management is planned, not a delivered feature.

steps.title: Keep a separate backup of your memory card
steps.instruction: Normal memory-card saves, settings and the crash log are outside the runtime: %APPDATA%/rerac on Windows, $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/rerac or ~/.config/rerac on Linux, and ~/Library/Application Support/rerac on macOS. Back up the profile you actually use separately. A custom RC_SAVE_DIR or RC_SETTINGS_FILE changes it. The launcher’s movable data/version/log folder can be different from the engine’s save/settings folder; preserve both when using it. Older versions may not read newer saves. Keep your original ISO and current working copy before re-extraction or changing versions.

steps.title: Select your own Glover ROM on first Play
steps.instruction: Choose Play, then select your own unmodified Glover USA revision 0 ROM when the game asks. The launcher accepts .z64, .n64 and .v64 byte order for this 8 MiB NGVE cartridge (canonical SHA-1 270be17b3c8da9b88a7b99c2a545b0bce16837f4). The published Windows player needs no game build or separate installer. Configure controls in the launcher or press F1/Escape while playing; use its Mods page for compatible mods and separate mod profiles.

steps.title: Keep your saves and mod profiles safe
steps.instruction: Default Windows saves, settings, mod profiles, mod-specific saves, logs and crash reports use %APPDATA%/Glover-R. Keep a separate backup of that profile before changing versions; an older runtime may not read newer data. Optional custom configuration and developer paths need their own backup. Keep customized existing copies registered with their own launch details.

steps.title: Linux uses the upstream AppImage route
steps.instruction: Use the Linux x86-64 AppImage, or extract the Linux Portable archive and deliberately run Launch-Glover-R.sh. That archive contains an AppImage and wrapper, rather than a bare player with ordinary libraries. The wrapper uses AppImage extraction mode when a normal AppImage launch is unavailable. Steam Deck uses its separate x86-64 package and START-GLOVER-R.sh. Linux saves/settings normally use $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/glover-r or ~/.config/glover-r; preserve that actual profile separately. Follow upstream updates for this copy; the Windows managed route does not manage the Linux wrapper or infer device/gameplay support.

steps.title: Let the upstream launcher prepare your own game
steps.instruction: The recommended Windows download is the upstream lawn/Z3R Launcher setup package. Open that installer deliberately after downloading, then use its guided preparation. steps.instruction: Keep the complete prepared project, your original ROM, zelda3_assets.dat, zelda3.user.ini overrides, saves, custom sprites/shaders/MSU packs, and any randomizer YAML, seed/spoiler files or selected feature-asset folders separately backed up. steps.title: Regenerate matching assets when updating
steps.instruction: Let the selected upstream launcher manage its own project setup and updates. Preserve the old prepared copy and randomizer choices before regeneration; extracting clean ROM data after randomizing overwrites the randomized YAML. Portcove registers the prepared player without claiming Update, Backup or Rollback for these externally owned files. The related Python Z3R-Launcher and current lawn delivery are helpers for this same engine identity, not extra games. The launcher’s Updates action uses its matching platform installer or self-replacement route; keep that owner. Its download feed follows releases without a fixed tag in this listing.
